snippets.title: snp config.toml
snippets.notes: snp's own config file. Every key is optional — each one also has a command-line flag and an `SNP_*` environment variable, and precedence is flag > env > file > default. The file lives at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/snp/config.toml`, or `~/.config/snp/config.toml` when that is unset; point somewhere else with `--config` or `SNP_CONFIG`. `snp key show-path` prints where the encryption key lives.
snippets.body:
hostname = "snp"
owner = "you@example.com"
state_dir = "~/.local/share/snp"
log_level = "info"

# AI snippet generation: set ai_key to enable it. Any
# OpenAI-compatible endpoint works (ollama, llama.cpp, ...).
# ai_endpoint = "https://api.openai.com/v1"
# ai_model = "gpt-4o-mini"
# ai_key = ""

snippets.title: Copy a file into a directory
snippets.notes: `{{source}}` and `{{dest}}` are template variables (spec §4). Fill them in the Variables panel before copying, or save defaults there; `dest` defaults to the current directory.

snippets.title: Serve the current directory over HTTP
snippets.notes: Python's built-in static file server. It binds every interface unless you say otherwise, so this one is pinned to loopback — drop `--bind 127.0.0.1` only if you mean to expose the directory to your network.

snippets.title: What is listening on a port
snippets.notes: Lists the process holding a TCP port. `-n` and `-P` stop lsof from resolving host and port names, which keeps it fast and the output exact. Needs root (or `sudo`) to see processes owned by other users.
